title: Why RNITAI Trades Here: Expectations, Reverse DCF and Peer Reality
web_title: 7. Why RNITAI Trades Here: Expectations, Reverse DCF and Peer Reality
book_title: Chapter 7: The Price of Possibility — What Earnings Must Prove
question: What must RNIT deliver to justify the market’s earnings multiple, and what return remains if it does?

web_blocks.text: Valuation begins with a data boundary. The Indian market session is dated 12 November 2026, but the RNITAI-specific market-facts series’ last available BSE bar is 11 November at ₹88.99. That is the price used for this chapter’s holding and valuation arithmetic. The consumer stock snapshot separately displayed a ₹89.80 current-price field after the cutoff; it is not substituted into position values or target math. This one-session feed mismatch is disclosed in the run notes. Audited FY2026 basic EPS was ₹1.57, so ₹88.99 is approximately 56.7 times that EPS. The TTM multiple in the aligned consumer snapshot differs because it uses a different earnings window. Keep those denominators separate. [1] [34]

The company had 8,47,92,083 shares outstanding at 31 March 2026 after the NCLT-driven merger and fresh allotment. Applying the ledger mark produces an equity capitalization of about ₹754.56 crore. That scale matters because RNIT’s audited FY2026 revenue was ₹51.50 crore, PAT ₹12.02 crore, CFO ₹11.23 crore and fixed/intangible purchases ₹18.97 crore. The resulting business is profitable but spent more on asset creation than operations generated. The case for a premium multiple therefore relies on forward reuse, product revenue and collections that are not separately reported. [1] [2]

The earnings story is undeniably better than the first post-relisting year. Revenue grew from ₹32.23 crore in FY2025 to ₹51.50 crore in FY2026; PAT grew from ₹7.21 crore to ₹12.02 crore. Q2 FY2027 revenue was ₹16.41 crore and half-year revenue ₹24.26 crore, with half-year PAT ₹5.51 crore. That creates a plausible growth case. But valuation should price collected cash and repeatable margins, not just a high growth rate. H1 FY2027 CFO was negative ₹7.10 crore while receivables rose to ₹30.85 crore; reported profit and cash conversion moved in opposite directions. [1] [2] [3]

The peer screen is deliberately heterogeneous. eMudhra sells digital trust and identity services; Newgen sells enterprise workflow software; Genesys combines digital mapping and technology services; Vakrangee distributes assisted digital services through a physical network. None is a perfect facial-recognition peer, so use multiples as context rather than a target-setting shortcut. Their reported business histories, disclosure depth, capital needs and risk profiles differ. The target row’s last ledger bar predates the report cutoff by one session; several peer bars also vary by one session. The table uses the fact-aligned price series and the same consumer snapshot’s fundamental ratios, not intraday prices. [22] [33] [34]

web_blocks.caption: RNITAI and four listed structural comparators — latest available price bars aligned to the session ledger
web_blocks.takeaway: RNITAI’s premium is not a simple software-peer premium: its audited FCF is negative after development purchases and its product/recurring revenue mix is undisclosed. eMudhra has a much longer disclosed digital-trust record; Newgen is a mature workflow vendor; Vakrangee and Genesys show that technology labels do not protect earnings or technical structure. The table is a screening comparison, not a claim of identical business economics. [1] [22] [23] [33]

web_blocks.text: The comparison has three distinct lessons. eMudhra’s FY2026 annual report provides product, geography, customer and cash-flow segmentation; RNIT reports one combined operating segment. Newgen’s workflow franchise serves a wider enterprise-software market, yet its latest consumer snapshot showed falling reported growth and a Stage 4 tape. Genesys and Vakrangee also illustrate that smaller IT or e-governance labels can carry uneven earnings and capital-market structure. The relevant question is not whether RNIT is “cheaper” than one peer; it is whether it can disclose repeatable deployments, renewal revenue and cash conversion at a standard comparable with established platform businesses. [22] [33] [34]

A normal historical P/E band cannot be estimated responsibly. Autopal’s legacy years describe auto-related products, the firm entered CIRP, RNIT Solutions & Services was merged with an appointed date in FY2024, and the listed company restarted under a new board and business. That is not a single public-software earnings series. Two audited post-reset years are too few for a meaningful distribution of RNITAI’s own software multiple through a full cycle. The market is pricing a forward business that has not yet shown a long public record of stable margins, renewals or cash returns. [1] [2] [15] [17]

The classic reverse DCF is constrained by the starting point: FY2026 free cash flow after fixed and intangible purchases was negative ₹7.74 crore, and H1 FY2027 operating cash flow was also negative. Discounting a negative trailing cash flow into a positive equity value produces no useful unique implied growth rate. A transparent equity-cash-flow hurdle is more honest: under a simplified scenario with 25% annual FCF growth for five years, 14% cost of equity and 3% terminal growth, first-year positive FCF would need to be about ₹43.9 crore to support the current ₹754.56 crore equity value. Those are analyst assumptions, not management guidance, and the filed cash-flow statement’s treatment of some financing movements makes the model illustrative. [1] [3]

web_blocks.the_number: About ₹43.9 crore of first-year equity free cash flow is required in the illustrative reverse-cash-flow case.
web_blocks.how_calculated: A deterministic Python calculation discounts five annual cash flows growing at 25%, plus a 3% terminal-growth value, at a 14% cost of equity, and solves for the first-year cash flow that equals the ₹754.56 crore ledger-mark equity capitalization.
web_blocks.the_inputs: ₹88.99 last available RNITAI ledger bar; 8,47,92,083 FY2026 shares; ₹754.56 crore equity value; 25% five-year cash-flow growth; 14% discount rate; 3% perpetual growth. FY2026 FCF was negative ₹7.74 crore, not positive.
web_blocks.the_range: The required starting FCF is much higher than FY2026 CFO of ₹11.23 crore and the reported H1 FY2027 CFO of negative ₹7.10 crore. The gap is a valuation hurdle, not a claim that these assumptions are achievable.
web_blocks.if_off: If recurring software revenue, acceptance and collections improve, the future cash-flow path may exceed the base case. If project customization and receivables remain heavy, the multiple can compress before earnings catch up.

web_blocks.text: For an earnings cross-check, the ledger price divided by FY2026 reported EPS is 56.7x. A five-year investor seeking 15% annualized return while assuming the exit multiple falls to 35x would need roughly 26.6% annual EPS growth. That is mathematically possible for an early company scaling from a small base, but it must coexist with low dilution, rising cash conversion and product reuse. RNIT has not yet disclosed enough evidence to establish all three. The company’s 37.9% TTM sales growth in the consumer snapshot is supportive; it does not answer whether the cash or recurring contribution scales at the same rate. [1] [3] [34]

The 12-month scenario framework used in Chapter 9 sets a base value of ₹63, a bull value of ₹110 and a bear value of ₹31.40. These are scenario outputs, not broker targets. The base assumes a 35-times normalized FY2027 EPS of ₹1.80; the bull requires EPS of ₹2.50 and a 44-times multiple; the bear assumes EPS of ₹1.00 and a 31.4-times multiple. The base is below the ledger mark. A quality improvement alone would not make a purchase at any price rational; the entry must also have room for loss and an evidenced cash path. [1] [3]

The valuation verdict is therefore not “AI cannot be valuable.” It is that the public price already pays for a successful transition while investors still lack product-level revenue, subscription mix, renewal cohorts, top-customer exposure and a clean post-reset free-cash-flow record. The base case does not clear the current ledger mark, and the monitor band near the 200-DMA/base support sits above the base value. Even a pullback to chart support would not repair that fundamental asymmetry. New money should be rejected until the earnings base, valuation and cash conversion reconcile. [1] [3] [22]

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay. Value is what you get.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett, letter to partners, 20 January 1966 [36]

book_paragraphs: You and I should start with the price that can actually be defended. The cutoff is 12 November, but the market-facts file’s last available RNITAI BSE bar is 11 November at ₹88.99. That is the ledger mark used for the dossier’s valuation and holding arithmetic. The consumer snapshot also showed ₹89.80 after the cutoff; it is disclosed as a feed discrepancy, not used to update the position. At ₹88.99 and audited FY2026 EPS of ₹1.57, RNIT trades at about 56.7 times that year’s earnings. The TTM multiple differs because it includes a newer earnings window. [1] [34]

At the FY2026 share count of 8,47,92,083, the ledger price represents approximately ₹754.56 crore of equity value. This market value is large relative to a business that reported ₹51.50 crore revenue and ₹12.02 crore profit in FY2026. Growth can justify a premium, but growth has to become cash. Cash from operations was ₹11.23 crore, while fixed and intangible purchases were ₹18.97 crore. The resulting FCF after investment was negative ₹7.74 crore. A buyer is paying for an expected future business, not merely the last audited year. [1]

The comparison table is useful only if we respect its limits. eMudhra sells digital trust, certificates and identity products; Newgen focuses on enterprise workflow software; Genesys has mapping and technology services; Vakrangee’s assisted service network is another route into digital governance. Their markets, customer mix and operating histories are not identical. But eMudhra’s annual report discloses customer count, line-of-business mix, geography and cash generation; RNIT’s statements aggregate its offerings into one operating segment. The gap is not cosmetic. It determines whether you can estimate recurring revenue and product-level returns. [22] [33] [34]

A historical valuation band is not available. Autopal’s legacy business, the CIRP and merger, the reconstituted share capital, and RNIT’s new software operation make old market prices and old earnings incomparable. You cannot read a stable “normal P/E” from a series that changes what the company sells. Two audited years of post-reset software statements are evidence that the operation exists; they are not yet a full-cycle sample. [1] [2] [15]

A conventional reverse DCF begins in the wrong place when trailing free cash flow is negative. FY2026 capex exceeded CFO, and the interim half-year cash flow then turned negative. So we ask a narrower question: what positive cash flow would make this equity value plausible? Under a transparent 25% annual cash-flow growth path for five years, 14% cost of equity and 3% terminal growth, the simplified model needs about ₹43.9 crore of first-year equity FCF to support the ledger-mark capitalization. That is far above the recent cash record. It is a hurdle, not a prediction. [1] [3]

Now compare the hurdle with the accounts. FY2026 CFO was ₹11.23 crore and FY2026 FCF after the disclosed asset purchases was negative ₹7.74 crore. H1 FY2027 CFO was negative ₹7.10 crore. The H1 change may be explained by receivable timing, contract assets, investment in software, or a combination; the company has not provided a project-by-project receipt bridge. If accepted deployments generate recurring collections, the cash path could improve. If each project requires bespoke work and absorbs working capital, the market’s required growth becomes harder to earn. [1] [3]

There is another way to read the price. At the FY2026 EPS, the current multiple is 56.7x. If you demand a 15% annualized return over five years and assume a 35x exit multiple, EPS has to compound roughly 26.6% annually. RNIT’s consumer snapshot showed high trailing revenue growth, but revenue growth is only one input. It does not prove that EPS compounds at that rate after interest, taxes, dilution, receivable funding and product-development spending. This is the difference between a growth narrative and a return case. [1] [34]

The base value of ₹63 is intentionally not a promise of where the share will trade next month. It assumes normalized FY2027 EPS of ₹1.80 and a 35x exit multiple. The bull case of ₹110 requires ₹2.50 EPS and a 44x multiple; the bear value of ₹31.40 assumes ₹1.00 EPS and 31.4x. Weighted at 20%, 55% and 25%, respectively, the scenario value is ₹64.50, about 27.5% below the ₹88.99 ledger mark. You may assign different probabilities, but the exercise makes the expected-return burden visible. [1] [3]

The competitive examples make the boundary clearer. eMudhra’s FY2026 report describes a much broader trust-services platform and reports 1,374 customers, while Newgen and Genesys have their own mature disclosures and technical cycles. Vakrangee warns that an e-governance label by itself does not guarantee strong growth or returns. None sets a target for RNIT. They show what an investor can compare: recurring revenue, customer retention, margin, cash conversion and balance-sheet resilience. [22] [33]

The maxim “Price is what you pay. Value is what you get” is a useful restraint here. It does not say every expensive company is bad; it says the burden of proof rises with the price. RNIT can still grow into an attractive business, but you need evidence of paid usage, renewals, gross-to-cash conversion and stable per-share growth before paying today’s multiple. Until that evidence appears, a pullback alone is not a valuation thesis. [36]

The independent call is rejection for new capital. The business has promise and the price has optionality, but the base case sits below the current mark and the support zone does not deliver adequate base-case reward for risk. The next evidence that would change your mind is not another slogan: it is an audited cash-flow recovery, a disclosed recurring-revenue mix, collections from aged receivables, and product reuse across multiple customers. Then we can ask whether the price has also reset. [1] [3]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Growth is an input; cash is the proof
book_callouts.text: A growing sales line can be real and still fail to compound per-share value if receivables, development spending and dilution keep absorbing the proceeds.
